questions.explanation: Removing a product continually pulls the reaction to the right, as Le Chatelier's principle predicts.

questions.stem: Le Chatelier's principle states that when a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it
options: shifts so as to oppose the change
shifts so as to increase the change
questions.explanation: For example, adding heat favours the reaction that absorbs heat.

questions.stem: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), dH is negative. Which single change increases BOTH the rate of reaction and the equilibrium yield of SO3?
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the rate (more frequent collisions) and favours the side with fewer gas moles (2 compared with 3). A higher temperature raises the rate but lowers the yield, and a catalyst does not change the yield.

questions.stem: For the equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g), changing the pressure
options: shifts the equilibrium to the right
shifts the equilibrium to the left
has no effect on the position of equilibrium
questions.explanation: There are 2 moles of gas on each side, so pressure does not favour either direction.

questions.stem: Adding more of a reactant to a system at equilibrium will
options: shift the position of equilibrium to the left
shift the position of equilibrium to the right
questions.explanation: The system uses up some of the added reactant by forming more products.

questions.stem: The value of the equilibrium constant, Kc, for a given reaction can be changed only by changing the
questions.explanation: Changes in concentration or pressure move the position of equilibrium but leave Kc the same. Only temperature changes Kc.

questions.stem: Which test is used to identify hydrogen gas?
options: It burns with a squeaky pop when a lighted splint is held near it
It turns damp red litmus paper blue
questions.explanation: Hydrogen mixed with air explodes gently with a pop. Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.stem: In the laboratory, hydrogen made from zinc granules and dilute hydrochloric acid is usually collected
options: by upward displacement of air, because it is denser than air
over water, because it is only slightly soluble in water
in an open beaker over concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
by dissolving it in water and then boiling it off
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is almost insoluble in water, so it can be collected by displacing water. It is less dense than air, not denser.

questions.stem: Trioxonitrate(V) acid is not used to prepare hydrogen from metals because
options: it does not react with metals
it forms insoluble salts with all metals
it is an oxidising agent and oxidises any hydrogen formed to water, giving oxides of nitrogen instead
questions.explanation: HNO3 is a strong oxidising agent, so it gives nitrogen oxides rather than free hydrogen when it reacts with most metals.

questions.stem: Water gas, a source of hydrogen in industry, is a mixture of
questions.explanation: Water gas is made by passing steam over white-hot coke: C + H2O -> CO + H2.

questions.stem: Which of these is a major industrial use of hydrogen?
options: Hardening vegetable oils to make margarine
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the C=C bonds of oils (with a nickel catalyst) to make solid fats. It is also used in making ammonia.

questions.stem: When hydrogen is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, the black solid turns reddish-brown and droplets of water form. This shows that hydrogen is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen removes oxygen from CuO, leaving copper metal: CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O.

questions.stem: In the laboratory, chlorine is prepared by oxidising concentrated hydrochloric acid with
questions.explanation: MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2 (on warming).

questions.stem: In the laboratory preparation of chlorine, the gas is passed first through water and then through concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid. The water is used to remove
questions.explanation: HCl is very soluble in water and is removed first. The concentrated H2SO4 then dries the chlorine.

questions.stem: Moist chlorine bleaches dyes because
options: it reduces the dye to a colourless compound
it reacts with water to form oxochlorate(I) acid (HOCl), which oxidises the dye
questions.explanation: Cl2 + H2O -> HCl + HOCl. HOCl is a powerful oxidising agent. Dry chlorine does not bleach.

questions.stem: Which test confirms the presence of chloride ions in a solution?
options: A white precipitate forms with barium chloride solution
A brown ring forms with iron(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI)
The solution turns lime water milky
A white precipitate forms with silver trioxonitrate(V) solution in the presence of dilute trioxonitrate(V) acid
questions.explanation: Ag+ + Cl- -> AgCl, a white precipitate that dissolves in aqueous ammonia.

questions.stem: When chlorine is bubbled into potassium bromide solution, the solution turns orange. This happens because
options: bromine is more reactive than chlorine
chlorine is a stronger oxidising agent than bromine and displaces it
questions.explanation: Cl2 + 2Br- -> 2Cl- + Br2. The more reactive halogen oxidises the halide ions of a less reactive one.

questions.stem: The fountain experiment with hydrogen chloride gas shows that hydrogen chloride
questions.explanation: The gas dissolves so quickly that the pressure in the flask drops, and water is forced up as a fountain.

questions.stem: Chlorine is added to public water supplies in order to
questions.explanation: Chlorine is an effective disinfectant.

questions.stem: Dry hydrogen chloride gas does not turn dry blue litmus paper red because
options: it does not ionise when no water is present
questions.explanation: HCl only forms H3O+ ions when it reacts with water, so dry HCl shows no acidic properties.

questions.stem: In the laboratory, oxygen can be prepared by heating potassium trioxochlorate(V) with manganese(IV) oxide. What is the role of the manganese(IV) oxide?
options: It is the source of the oxygen
questions.explanation: 2KClO3 -> 2KCl + 3O2. MnO2 speeds up the decomposition and is left unchanged at the end.

questions.stem: Which test confirms that a gas is oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion strongly enough to rekindle a glowing splint.

questions.stem: Which of these oxides is acidic?
questions.explanation: SO2 dissolves in water to form H2SO3 and reacts with alkalis. MgO is basic, CO is neutral and Al2O3 is amphoteric.

questions.stem: Carbon(II) oxide is classified as
questions.explanation: CO does not react with acids or alkalis to form salts. Other neutral oxides include N2O, NO and H2O.

questions.stem: Which catalyst is used in the Contact process for making tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid?
questions.explanation: V2O5 catalyses 2SO2 + O2 <=> 2SO3 at about 450 °C.

questions.stem: In the Contact process, sulphur(VI) oxide is absorbed in concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid rather than directly in water because
options: sulphur(VI) oxide does not react with water
the reaction with water is very violent and forms a mist of acid that is hard to condense
water would reduce it back to sulphur(IV) oxide
the acid acts as a catalyst for the reaction
questions.explanation: SO3 is first absorbed to form oleum (H2S2O7), which is then carefully diluted with water.

questions.stem: When concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is added to sugar, a black mass of carbon forms. Here the acid is acting as
questions.explanation: It removes the elements of water from the carbohydrate, leaving carbon behind.

questions.stem: The two main crystalline allotropes of sulphur are
questions.explanation: Rhombic sulphur is stable below 96 °C and monoclinic sulphur above it. Plastic sulphur is amorphous, not crystalline.

questions.stem: Sulphur(IV) oxide bleaches moist coloured flowers by
questions.explanation: SO2 removes oxygen from the dye. The bleaching can be reversed slowly by air, unlike bleaching by chlorine, which works by oxidation.

questions.stem: A gas that smells of rotten eggs turns filter paper soaked in lead(II) ethanoate black. The gas is
questions.explanation: H2S reacts with Pb2+ to form black lead(II) sulphide, PbS.

questions.stem: In the laboratory, ammonia is usually prepared by heating ammonium chloride with
questions.explanation: An ammonium salt heated with an alkali releases ammonia: 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3.

questions.stem: Which drying agent is used for ammonia gas?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is basic, so it reacts with acidic drying agents. It also forms a compound with CaCl2. Quicklime is basic and does not react with it.

questions.stem: Ammonia is collected by upward delivery (downward displacement of air) because it is
options: denser than air and insoluble in water
less dense than air and insoluble in water
denser than air and very soluble in water
less dense than air and very soluble in water
questions.explanation: It cannot be collected over water because it is very soluble. Being lighter than air, it collects at the top of an inverted jar.

questions.stem: What is the catalyst in the Haber process for making ammonia?
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron catalyses N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3 at about 450 °C and 200 atm.

questions.stem: Which observation confirms that a gas is ammonia?
options: It turns damp red litmus paper blue and forms dense white fumes with hydrogen chloride
It turns damp blue litmus paper red
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the only common alkaline gas. With HCl it forms white fumes of NH4Cl.

questions.stem: In the Ostwald process, ammonia is catalytically oxidised as the first step in the manufacture of
questions.explanation: 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O over Pt-Rh. The NO is then converted to NO2, and NO2 to HNO3.

questions.stem: What are the products when copper(II) trioxonitrate(V) is heated strongly?
options: Copper(II) oxide, nitrogen(IV) oxide and oxygen
questions.explanation: 2Cu(NO3)2 -> 2CuO + 4NO2 + O2. Only the nitrates of the most reactive metals (Na, K) form the dioxonitrate(III) and oxygen.

questions.stem: The brown ring test is used to detect
questions.explanation: Freshly made FeSO4 and concentrated H2SO4 produce a brown ring where they meet a solution containing nitrate ions.

questions.stem: Nitrogen is used to fill packets of snacks because it
options: kills all bacteria by poisoning them
is unreactive and keeps out oxygen, which would make the food go stale
questions.explanation: An inert atmosphere slows oxidation (rancidity) and the growth of aerobic microbes.

questions.stem: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in the fertiliser ammonium tetraoxosulphate(VI), (NH4)2SO4? (N = 14, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Mr = 2(18) + 96 = 132, and the mass of nitrogen is 28. 28/132 x 100 = 21.2%.

questions.stem: Which pair of substances are both allotropes of carbon?
questions.explanation: Allotropes are different forms of the same element in the same physical state. Limestone and CO2 are compounds.

questions.stem: Graphite is used as a dry lubricant because
options: its layers can slide easily over one another
it has a very low melting point
questions.explanation: Only weak forces hold the layers of graphite together.

questions.stem: Carbon(IV) oxide is prepared in the laboratory from marble chips and dilute hydrochloric acid, not dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, because with the latter
options: no gas is produced at all
the gas produced is sulphur(IV) oxide
insoluble calcium tetraoxosulphate(VI) coats the marble and stops the reaction
questions.explanation: CaSO4 is only slightly soluble, so it forms a layer over the marble that keeps the acid away.

questions.stem: When carbon(IV) oxide is bubbled through lime water for a long time, the milkiness first appears and then disappears. It disappears because
questions.explanation: CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 -> Ca(HCO3)2, which is soluble.

questions.stem: In the blast furnace and in other metal extractions, carbon(II) oxide is used as
questions.explanation: CO removes oxygen from metal oxides, for example Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2.

questions.stem: Carbon(IV) oxide is used in fire extinguishers because it
options: is denser than air and does not support combustion
is less dense than air and burns
reacts with oxygen to form carbon(II) oxide
questions.explanation: It sinks over the fire and cuts off the supply of oxygen.

questions.stem: What is formed when sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) (baking soda) is heated?
options: Sodium oxide and carbon(IV) oxide only
Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), water and carbon(IV) oxide
Sodium metal, hydrogen and carbon(IV) oxide
questions.explanation: 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2. The CO2 given off makes dough rise.

questions.stem: Which of these trioxocarbonate(IV) salts is NOT decomposed by the heat of a Bunsen burner?
questions.explanation: The carbonates of sodium and potassium are thermally stable. Other carbonates decompose to the oxide and CO2.

questions.stem: Heating coal strongly in the absence of air to produce coke, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor and coal gas is called
questions.explanation: Without air the coal decomposes instead of burning, and the volatile products are collected.

questions.stem: Activated charcoal is used in refining sugar because it
options: acts as a catalyst for crystallisation
questions.explanation: The very large surface area of activated charcoal holds coloured molecules on its surface.

questions.stem: Which of these is a general property of metals?
options: They are good conductors of heat and electricity
They have low densities and low melting points
questions.explanation: Delocalised electrons make metals good conductors. Metal oxides are usually basic.

questions.stem: Metals usually form positive ions because
options: they have few valence electrons, which they lose easily
questions.explanation: Losing one, two or three electrons gives a stable noble-gas arrangement.

questions.stem: Very reactive metals such as sodium and potassium are extracted by
questions.explanation: Their ions are too stable to be reduced by carbon, so electrolysis is needed.

questions.stem: Which of these metals is extracted by reducing its oxide with carbon?
questions.explanation: Iron is below carbon in the reactivity series, so coke (as CO) can reduce iron ore. The others are extracted by electrolysis.

questions.stem: Metals can be hammered into sheets (they are malleable) because
options: metals contain ions of opposite charges
metal atoms are joined by covalent bonds
layers of metal ions can slide over one another without the metallic bond breaking
questions.explanation: The sea of delocalised electrons keeps holding the ions together as the layers move.

questions.stem: Sodium is stored under kerosene because it
options: reacts readily with air and water
questions.explanation: Kerosene keeps oxygen and moisture away from the very reactive metal.

questions.stem: What are the products when sodium reacts with cold water?
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2. The solution formed is alkaline.

questions.stem: What are the main raw materials of the Solvay process for making sodium trioxocarbonate(IV)?
questions.explanation: CO2 from limestone is passed into ammoniated brine to precipitate NaHCO3, which is then heated to give Na2CO3. The ammonia is recycled.

questions.stem: Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) is used on a large scale in the manufacture of
questions.explanation: Glass is made by fusing sand, Na2CO3 and limestone.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide solution is added drop by drop to a solution containing a metal ion. A white precipitate forms and dissolves when excess sodium hydroxide is added. Which ion could be present?
questions.explanation: Zinc hydroxide is amphoteric and dissolves in excess alkali. Ca(OH)2 stays as a white precipitate, Fe(OH)2 is green and Cu(OH)2 is blue.

questions.stem: What colour do sodium compounds give to a non-luminous flame?
questions.explanation: Sodium gives a persistent golden-yellow flame. Potassium gives lilac.

questions.stem: Quicklime (calcium oxide) is manufactured by
questions.explanation: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 in a lime kiln.

questions.stem: Farmers add slaked lime, Ca(OH)2, to soil in order to
options: reduce the acidity of the soil
increase the acidity of the soil
questions.explanation: The base neutralises excess acid in the soil.

questions.stem: What colour do calcium compounds give to a flame?
questions.explanation: Ca2+ gives a brick-red (orange-red) flame.

questions.stem: Plaster of Paris is made by
options: partly removing the water of crystallisation from gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) by heating
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is (CaSO4)2.H2O. It sets into a hard mass when it is mixed with water.

questions.stem: A clear solution of calcium hydroxide in water is known as
questions.explanation: Lime water is a saturated solution of Ca(OH)2. Milk of lime is a suspension of it.

questions.stem: What is the chief ore from which aluminium is extracted?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide. Haematite is an iron ore, cassiterite a tin ore and galena a lead ore.

questions.stem: In the extraction of aluminium, purified alumina is dissolved in molten cryolite in order to
options: lower the melting point of the electrolyte and improve its conductivity
questions.explanation: Alumina melts at about 2000 °C. Dissolving it in cryolite allows electrolysis at about 950 °C, which saves energy.

questions.stem: Aluminium is used for window frames and cooking pots, even though it is a reactive metal, because
options: it is below hydrogen in the electrochemical series
it does not react with oxygen
a thin, unreactive layer of oxide forms on its surface and protects it
it is always coated with paint
questions.explanation: The Al2O3 layer sticks firmly to the metal and stops further corrosion.

questions.stem: During the electrolytic extraction of aluminium, the carbon anodes have to be replaced regularly because
options: they are burnt away by the oxygen given off at them
they are reduced to carbon(II) oxide by the aluminium
questions.explanation: Oxygen released at the hot anodes reacts with the carbon to form CO2.

questions.stem: The main ore of tin, mined on the Jos Plateau in Nigeria, is
questions.explanation: Cassiterite (tin(IV) oxide) is reduced with carbon to obtain tin.

questions.stem: Steel food cans are coated with tin because tin
options: is a good conductor of heat
is unreactive towards food acids and is non-toxic
questions.explanation: Tin forms a protective barrier, as long as the coating is not broken.

questions.stem: If a tin-plated steel can is scratched, the exposed iron rusts quickly because
options: iron is more reactive than tin, so the iron corrodes in preference to the tin
tin is more reactive than iron
tin catalyses the reaction of oxygen with water
questions.explanation: In the tin-iron cell that forms at the scratch, iron is the anode and is oxidised, so the tin speeds up the rusting. Zinc coating works the other way.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Which of these properties is typical of transition metals?
options: They have only one oxidation state
They show variable oxidation states and form coloured compounds
They are soft metals with low densities
questions.explanation: Partly filled d orbitals give transition metals several oxidation states, coloured ions and catalytic activity.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Which of these ions is green in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Hydrated Fe2+ is pale green and Cu2+ is blue. Zn2+ and Na+ are colourless.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: What is the ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (atomic number 24)?
questions.explanation: A half-filled d sub-level is especially stable, so one 4s electron moves into 3d.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a transition metal used as a catalyst?
questions.explanation: Iron catalyses the synthesis of ammonia. The Contact process uses V2O5 and the Ostwald process uses Pt-Rh.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Zinc is often described as not being a typical transition metal because
options: its only ion, Zn2+, has a completely filled d sub-level
it has no d electrons at all
it is not in the d-block
questions.explanation: With a full 3d^10 sub-level, Zn2+ forms colourless compounds and shows only one oxidation state.

questions.stem: In the blast furnace, limestone is added to the charge in order to
questions.explanation: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, and then CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 (slag), which floats on the molten iron.

questions.stem: What is the main reducing agent in the blast furnace?
questions.explanation: Coke burns to CO2, which reacts with more coke to form CO. The CO then reduces Fe2O3 to iron.

questions.stem: What is the formula of haematite, the main ore of iron?
questions.explanation: Haematite is iron(III) oxide. Fe3O4 is magnetite and FeCO3 is siderite.

questions.stem: Cast (pig) iron is hard but brittle because it
options: contains a high proportion of carbon
questions.explanation: Cast iron contains about 3 to 4% carbon. Lowering the carbon content gives tougher steel.

questions.stem: When sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution of an iron(II) salt, the precipitate formed is
questions.explanation: Fe(OH)2 is a dirty green precipitate. Iron(III) salts give a reddish-brown precipitate of Fe(OH)3.

questions.stem: Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of iron(III) chloride. What is observed?
options: A green precipitate that dissolves in excess alkali
A reddish-brown precipitate that does not dissolve in excess alkali
A white precipitate that dissolves in excess alkali
questions.explanation: Fe3+ + 3OH- -> Fe(OH)3, which is reddish-brown and not amphoteric.

questions.stem: Copper reacts with dilute trioxonitrate(V) acid to give copper(II) trioxonitrate(V), water and
questions.explanation: 3Cu + 8HNO3(dilute) -> 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O. Copper cannot displace hydrogen from acids.

questions.stem: When copper reacts with concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid, the brown gas given off is
questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO3 is reduced to brown NO2.

questions.stem: Copper roofs slowly develop a green coating. The coating is mainly
questions.explanation: Copper reacts slowly with oxygen, water and CO2 in the air to form CuCO3.Cu(OH)2 (verdigris).

questions.stem: Excess aqueous ammonia is added to a solution of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI). What is observed?
options: A pale blue precipitate forms and then dissolves to give a deep blue solution
A white precipitate forms that does not dissolve
questions.explanation: Cu(OH)2 forms first. It dissolves in excess ammonia to form the deep blue [Cu(NH3)4]2+ complex ion.

questions.stem: Copper is widely used for electrical wiring because it
options: is an excellent conductor of electricity and is ductile
questions.explanation: Copper conducts electricity very well and can easily be drawn into wires.

questions.stem: Brass is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brass is copper and zinc. Bronze is copper and tin.

questions.stem: Bronze is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Bronze is harder than copper and resists corrosion. It is used for statues and medals.

questions.stem: Steel is an alloy of iron with a small amount of
questions.explanation: Mild steel contains up to about 0.25% carbon. Higher carbon contents give harder steels.

questions.stem: Duralumin is used in building aircraft because it is
options: a very good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Duralumin is mostly aluminium with copper, magnesium and manganese, which make it stronger than pure aluminium.

questions.stem: Solder, used for joining electrical wires, is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Solder has a low melting point, which makes it suitable for joining metal parts.

questions.stem: Stainless steel resists rusting because it contains iron alloyed with
questions.explanation: Chromium forms a protective oxide layer on the surface.

questions.stem: Carbon forms a very large number of compounds mainly because carbon atoms
options: are tetravalent and can join to one another to form chains and rings (catenation)
have a high relative atomic mass
questions.explanation: Four bonds per atom and strong C-C bonds allow almost endless chains, branches and rings.

questions.stem: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated: every carbon has its full share of hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: What is the functional group of the alkanols?
questions.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols) contain the -OH group attached to an alkyl group.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane), and the methyl group is on carbon 2 when counting from the end nearest the branch.

questions.stem: Structural isomers are compounds that have
options: the same structural formula but different molecular formulae
the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
questions.explanation: For example, butane and 2-methylpropane are both C4H10.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C5H12?
questions.explanation: They are pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.stem: Along a homologous series, which property changes gradually as the number of carbon atoms increases?
questions.explanation: Members share a functional group and general formula, but their physical properties, such as boiling point, change steadily.

questions.stem: 0.30 g of an organic compound containing only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen burned completely to give 0.44 g of CO2 and 0.18 g of H2O. What is its empirical formula? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
An organic compound with the molecular formula C2H4O2 turns blue litmus red and gives off CO2 with sodium trioxocarbonate(IV). The compound is
questions.explanation: Only the alkanoic acid releases CO2 from carbonates. Methyl methanoate is an isomer, but it is a neutral ester.

questions.stem: The reaction between methane and chlorine in sunlight is an example of
questions.explanation: Chlorine atoms replace hydrogen atoms one at a time (CH3Cl, CH2Cl2 and so on), and HCl is formed.

questions.stem: Alkanes are described as saturated hydrocarbons because they
options: contain only single bonds between carbon atoms
questions.explanation: Each carbon forms four single bonds, so no more atoms can be added.

questions.stem: The main constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation: Natural gas, such as that produced in the Niger Delta, is mostly methane.

questions.stem: The boiling points of straight-chain alkanes increase as the chain gets longer because
options: the van der Waals forces between molecules increase with molecular size
questions.explanation: Larger molecules have more electrons and more surface contact, so the intermolecular forces are stronger.

questions.stem: Pentane boils at a higher temperature than 2,2-dimethylpropane, although both are C5H12, because
options: the straight-chain molecule has a larger surface area for intermolecular attraction
questions.explanation: Compact, branched molecules touch each other less, so the van der Waals forces between them are weaker.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C6H14?
questions.explanation: They are hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.stem: What are the products of the complete combustion of propane?
In the laboratory, methane can be prepared by heating sodium ethanoate with
questions.explanation: CH3COONa + NaOH -> CH4 + Na2CO3. Soda lime supplies the NaOH.

questions.stem: Trichloromethane, a halogenated derivative of methane, was once widely used as
questions.explanation: Trichloromethane (chloroform) is an example of a useful halogenated alkane, although it is no longer used as an anaesthetic because it is toxic.

questions.stem: Which fraction of crude oil is used as fuel for jet aircraft?
questions.explanation: Kerosene (paraffin) is used as aviation fuel and for lamps and stoves.

questions.stem: In the fractional distillation of crude oil, which fraction has the lowest boiling range and is collected at the top of the column?
questions.explanation: The smallest molecules (C1 to C4) have the weakest intermolecular forces, so they rise highest.

questions.stem: Cracking in the petroleum industry is
options: the joining together of small molecules
the separation of crude oil into fractions
the breaking down of large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones
the removal of sulphur from crude oil
questions.explanation: Heavy fractions are cracked by heat and catalysts to give more petrol and alkenes such as ethene.

questions.stem: The octane number of a petrol is a measure of its
options: resistance to knocking in an engine
questions.explanation: It compares the petrol with 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (octane number 100) and heptane (octane number 0).

questions.stem: Bitumen, the residue from the fractional distillation of crude oil, is mainly used for
questions.explanation: Bitumen is thick and sticky. It binds the stones in tarred roads and is used in roofing.

questions.stem: Reforming improves the quality of petrol by
options: converting straight-chain alkanes into branched-chain and aromatic hydrocarbons
questions.explanation: Branched and aromatic hydrocarbons burn more smoothly, which raises the octane number.

questions.stem: A simple test that shows a hydrocarbon is unsaturated is that it
questions.explanation: Bromine adds across the C=C double bond, so the orange-brown colour disappears.

questions.stem: Ethene is prepared in the laboratory by heating ethanol with
options: excess concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid at about 170 °C
questions.explanation: The concentrated acid removes water from ethanol: C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O.

questions.stem: When ethene and hydrogen are passed over a heated nickel catalyst, the product is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the double bond (hydrogenation).

questions.stem: The addition polymerisation of ethene produces
questions.explanation: Many ethene molecules join together by opening their double bonds to form -(CH2-CH2)n-.

questions.stem: Which hydrocarbon is used to speed up the ripening of fruits such as bananas?
questions.explanation: Ethene is a natural plant hormone that triggers ripening.

questions.stem: The vulcanisation of rubber involves heating the rubber with
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links between the polymer chains, which makes the rubber harder and more elastic.

questions.stem: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explanation: One C=C double bond means two fewer hydrogen atoms than in the corresponding alkane.

questions.stem: When hydrogen bromide adds to propene, CH3CH=CH2, what is the major product?
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule, the hydrogen adds to the carbon that already has more hydrogens, and the Br goes to the middle carbon.

questions.stem: Ethyne is prepared in the laboratory by the action of water on
questions.explanation: CaC2 + 2H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + C2H2.

questions.stem: Which hydrocarbon, when burnt in pure oxygen, gives a flame hot enough to cut through steel?
questions.explanation: The oxy-ethyne (oxy-acetylene) flame reaches about 3000 °C.

questions.stem: A terminal alkyne such as ethyne can be distinguished from an alkene because it
options: forms a red-brown precipitate with ammoniacal copper(I) chloride
is a gas at room temperature
questions.explanation: Alkenes also decolourise bromine water. Only terminal alkynes (with an H on the triple-bonded carbon) form metal acetylides.

questions.stem: What is the general formula of the alkynes?
questions.explanation: A triple bond means four fewer hydrogen atoms than in the corresponding alkane.

questions.stem: Ethyne reacts with excess hydrogen over a nickel catalyst to give
questions.explanation: Two moles of H2 add across the triple bond: C2H2 + 2H2 -> C2H6.

questions.stem: Benzene undergoes substitution reactions more readily than addition reactions because
options: its delocalised electrons make the ring very stable
it has three isolated double bonds
questions.explanation: Addition would destroy the stable delocalised system, but substitution keeps it.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of benzene?
questions.explanation: Benzene is a six-carbon ring with one hydrogen on each carbon.

questions.stem: Benzene burns with a very smoky (sooty) flame because
options: it has a high ratio of carbon to hydrogen
it has a low boiling point
questions.explanation: There is not enough oxygen to burn all the carbon, so unburnt carbon particles form soot.

questions.stem: The nitration of benzene is carried out using
options: nitrogen gas and a nickel catalyst
a mixture of concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid and concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
questions.explanation: The mixed acids produce the NO2+ ion, which substitutes a hydrogen on the ring to give nitrobenzene.

questions.stem: The fermentation of glucose by yeast produces ethanol and
questions.explanation: C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2, catalysed by enzymes in yeast.

questions.stem: Which enzyme in yeast converts glucose into ethanol?
questions.explanation: Diastase turns starch into maltose, maltase turns maltose into glucose, and zymase turns glucose into ethanol.

questions.stem: 2-methylpropan-2-ol, (CH3)3COH, is classified as
questions.explanation: The carbon carrying the -OH group is bonded to three other carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH3, is classified as
questions.explanation: The -OH carbon is attached to two other carbon atoms.

questions.stem: When ethanol is heated under reflux with excess acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI), the main organic product is
questions.explanation: A primary alkanol is oxidised first to the alkanal and then, under reflux, to the alkanoic acid.

questions.stem: A piece of sodium is dropped into ethanol. The gas given off is
questions.explanation: 2C2H5OH + 2Na -> 2C2H5ONa + H2. The reaction is slower than that of sodium with water.

questions.stem: Illegally distilled gin is sometimes contaminated with methanol, which is dangerous because methanol
options: is poisonous and can cause blindness or death
cannot be absorbed by the body
questions.explanation: Methanol is metabolised to methanal and methanoic acid, which damage the optic nerve.

questions.stem: Ethanol made from crops such as cassava or sugar cane is blended with petrol as an alternative fuel because it
options: has a higher energy content than petrol
questions.explanation: Ethanol made by fermentation can be replaced by growing more crops, and it burns with little soot.

questions.stem: The controlled (partial) oxidation of a primary alkanol first gives
questions.explanation: Primary alkanols give alkanals (aldehydes), which can be oxidised further to acids. Secondary alkanols give alkanones.

questions.stem: What is formed when propan-2-ol is oxidised with acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI)?
questions.explanation: Secondary alkanols are oxidised to alkanones, which resist further oxidation.

questions.stem: An alkanal can be distinguished from an alkanone by warming each with Fehling's solution, because
options: the alkanone gives a brick-red precipitate but the alkanal does not
the alkanal gives a brick-red precipitate but the alkanone does not react
questions.explanation: Alkanals are reducing agents and reduce Cu2+ to Cu2O. Alkanones are not easily oxidised.

questions.stem: In alkanones, the carbonyl group (C=O) is
options: bonded to at least one hydrogen atom
at the end of the carbon chain
questions.explanation: In propanone, CH3COCH3, the C=O group is in the middle of the chain. In alkanals it is at the end, attached to an H.

questions.stem: A solution of methanal (formalin) is used for
questions.explanation: Methanal kills micro-organisms and hardens tissues.

questions.stem: Vinegar is a dilute solution of
questions.explanation: Vinegar contains about 4 to 8% ethanoic acid.

questions.stem: What is the functional group of the alkanoic acids?
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group gives these compounds their acidic properties.

questions.stem: Ethanedioic acid, HOOC-COOH, is described as dibasic because
options: it reacts with two different bases
each molecule has two replaceable hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: Both -COOH groups can lose H+, giving salts such as sodium ethanedioate.

questions.stem: The sting of an ant contains
questions.explanation: Methanoic acid (formic acid, from the Latin word for ant) causes the stinging pain.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid is described as a weak acid because
options: it does not react with metals
it is only partly ionised in water
questions.explanation: Only a small fraction of CH3COOH molecules ionise into CH3COO- and H3O+.

questions.stem: Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of a little concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to form
questions.explanation: This is esterification. The acid catalyses the reaction and removes the water formed.

questions.stem: Esters (alkanoates) are commonly used in
options: perfumes and food flavourings, because of their sweet fruity smells
questions.explanation: Many natural fruit scents are esters.

questions.stem: Saponification is
options: the formation of an ester from an acid and an alcohol
the hydrolysis of fats or oils by an alkali to give soap and propane-1,2,3-triol
the hardening of oils by hydrogen
questions.explanation: Boiling an oil such as palm oil with NaOH gives sodium salts of fatty acids (soap) and glycerol.

questions.stem: An advantage of soapless detergents over soap is that they
options: are made from vegetable oils only
do not form scum with hard water
questions.explanation: Their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble, so they lather well even in hard water.

questions.stem: Margarine is made from vegetable oils by
options: boiling the oils with sodium hydroxide
cracking the oils at high temperature
adding hydrogen to the oils in the presence of a nickel catalyst
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation saturates some of the C=C bonds, which raises the melting point so the fat is solid at room temperature.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH3COOCH3?
questions.explanation: The acid part (CH3COO-) is ethanoate and the alcohol part (-CH3) is methyl.

questions.stem: Palm oil is chemically
options: a mixture of esters of propane-1,2,3-triol and long-chain fatty acids
questions.explanation: Fats and oils are triglycerides (triesters of glycerol).

questions.stem: Amines behave as bases because
options: the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom can accept a proton
questions.explanation: Like ammonia, RNH2 + H2O <=> RNH3+ + OH-.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH3NH2?
questions.explanation: An -NH2 group attached to a methyl group gives methanamine (methylamine).

questions.stem: Dimethylamine, (CH3)2NH, is classified as
questions.explanation: The nitrogen atom is bonded to two carbon groups.

questions.stem: Simple amines such as methanamine have a smell like that of
questions.explanation: Low-molecular-mass amines have a characteristic fishy smell.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a monosaccharide. C12H22O11 is a disaccharide such as sucrose, and (C6H10O5)n is starch.

questions.stem: What are the products of the complete hydrolysis of sucrose?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide made of one glucose unit and one fructose unit.

questions.stem: Which reagent gives a blue-black colour with starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine fits inside the coiled starch molecule and gives an intense blue-black colour.

questions.stem: Which reagent gives a brick-red precipitate when warmed with a reducing sugar such as glucose?
questions.explanation: Reducing sugars reduce blue Cu2+ to red copper(I) oxide.

questions.stem: Cellulose, the main material of plant cell walls, is a polymer of
questions.explanation: Both starch and cellulose are polysaccharides made of glucose units, joined together in different ways.

questions.stem: The hydrolysis of maltose gives
questions.explanation: Maltose is a disaccharide of two glucose units.

questions.stem: Proteins are polymers of
questions.explanation: Amino acids are joined together by peptide bonds.

questions.stem: The linkage joining amino acid units together in proteins is the
questions.explanation: It forms by condensation between the -COOH group of one amino acid and the -NH2 group of the next.

questions.stem: In the biuret test, a protein solution gives
questions.explanation: Copper(II) ions in alkaline solution form a violet complex with peptide bonds.

questions.stem: When concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid is added to egg white and the mixture is warmed, the colour that forms is
questions.explanation: This is the xanthoproteic test, which detects aromatic amino acid units in proteins.

questions.stem: The complete hydrolysis of a protein by boiling with dilute acid gives
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis breaks the peptide bonds and releases the individual amino acids.

questions.stem: Which of these is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Natural rubber comes from the latex of rubber trees. The others are synthetic.

questions.stem: Nylon is formed by
questions.explanation: Each time two monomer units link together, a small molecule such as water is eliminated.

questions.stem: Which of these is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Bakelite sets permanently when heated because it has a cross-linked structure. The others are thermoplastics.

questions.stem: Thermoplastics are polymers that
options: soften when heated and can be remoulded many times
questions.explanation: Their chains are not cross-linked, so they can slide past one another when warm.

questions.stem: What is the monomer of polyvinyl chloride (PVC)?
questions.explanation: Chloroethene, CH2=CHCl, undergoes addition polymerisation.

questions.stem: A sample of polythene has a relative molecular mass of 28 000. About how many ethene units are there in each chain? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Ethene, C2H4, has Mr = 28, and 28 000/28 = 1000.

questions.stem: Terylene, used in making clothing, is an example of
questions.explanation: Terylene is made by condensation between a diol and a dicarboxylic acid, forming ester linkages.

questions.stem: What are the main raw materials for making cement?
questions.explanation: Limestone and clay (or shale) are heated in a kiln to form clinker, which is then ground with gypsum.

questions.stem: Which is an example of biotechnology in chemical industry?
options: Making steel in a blast furnace
Using yeast to ferment cassava starch or sugar into ethanol
questions.explanation: Biotechnology uses living organisms or their enzymes to make products.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a heavy chemical industry?
questions.explanation: Heavy chemicals are basic substances made in very large tonnages. Fine chemicals are made in small amounts and need high purity.

questions.stem: Ordinary soda glass is made by melting together
questions.explanation: Silica, soda ash and lime fuse to form soda-lime glass.

questions.stem: Which pair of raw materials is used to make soap in a factory?
questions.explanation: Saponification of oils such as palm or palm-kernel oil with caustic soda gives soap.

questions.stem: Most of the hydrogen needed to make ammonia for fertilisers is obtained from
questions.explanation: Steam reforming: CH4 + H2O -> CO + 3H2. Nigeria has large natural gas reserves for this.

questions.stem: Which of these is a disadvantage of siting a chemical industry close to a town?
options: It may pollute the air and water around it
It provides jobs for local people
It brings in revenue for the government
It encourages the building of roads
questions.explanation: The other three are benefits. Pollution is the main environmental cost.

questions.stem: What mass of sodium hydroxide is needed to neutralise 49 g of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid completely? H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23, S = 32)
questions.explanation: 49/98 = 0.5 mol of H2SO4, which needs 1.0 mol of NaOH = 40 g. 20 g ignores the 1:2 ratio.

questions.stem: What mass of iron can be obtained by completely reducing 320 g of iron(III) oxide? Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2 (Fe = 56, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Fe2O3 = 160 g/mol, so 320 g = 2.0 mol. This gives 4.0 mol of Fe, and 4.0 x 56 = 224 g.

questions.stem: How many moles of ions are present in 0.10 mol of aluminium tetraoxosulphate(VI), Al2(SO4)3, if it ionises completely?
questions.explanation: Each formula unit gives 2Al3+ + 3SO4 2-, which is 5 ions. 0.10 x 5 = 0.50 mol.

questions.stem: When 10.0 g of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) was heated, 4.2 g of calcium oxide was obtained. What is the percentage yield? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: The theoretical yield is 10.0 x 56/100 = 5.6 g, so the percentage yield = 4.2/5.6 x 100 = 75%.

questions.stem: What volume of carbon(IV) oxide, measured at s.t.p., is given off when 10.6 g of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid? (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3)
questions.explanation: Na2CO3 = 106 g/mol, so 10.6 g = 0.10 mol, which gives 0.10 mol of CO2 = 2.24 dm^3.

questions.stem: A gas occupies 150 cm^3 at 91 °C and 380 mmHg. What is its volume at s.t.p. (0 °C and 760 mmHg)?
questions.explanation: V2 = 150 x (380/760) x (273/364) = 56.3 cm^3. Both the drop in pressure and the cooling must be taken into account.

questions.stem: 100 cm^3 of oxygen diffuses through a small hole in 20 s. Under the same conditions, how long will 100 cm^3 of sulphur(IV) oxide take to diffuse through the same hole? (O = 16, S = 32)
questions.explanation: Time is proportional to sqrt(M): t = 20 x sqrt(64/32) = 20 x 1.414 = 28.3 s.

questions.stem: How many molecules are there in 1.12 dm^3 of a gas at s.t.p.? (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3; Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23 mol^-1)
The solubility of potassium chloride at 20 °C is 34 g per 100 g of water. What mass of potassium chloride is dissolved in 67 g of the saturated solution at 20 °C?
questions.explanation: 134 g of saturated solution contains 34 g of KCl, so 67 g contains 67 x 34/134 = 17 g. 22.8 g wrongly treats 67 g of solution as 67 g of water.

questions.stem: 7.45 g of potassium chloride just saturates 50 cm^3 of solution at a certain temperature. What is the solubility of KCl at that temperature in mol dm^-3? (K = 39, Cl = 35.5)
0.40 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water and made up to 1.0 dm^3 of solution. What is the pH of the solution at 25 °C? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
What is the pH of 0.005 mol dm^-3 tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, assuming that it ionises completely?
questions.explanation: Each H2SO4 gives 2H+, so [H+] = 0.010 mol dm^-3 and pH = 2. The answer 2.3 forgets that the acid is dibasic.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm^3 of 0.10 mol dm^-3 sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution required 20.0 cm^3 of hydrochloric acid for complete neutralisation. Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. What is the concentration of the acid?
questions.explanation: Na2CO3 = 0.0025 mol, so HCl = 0.0050 mol in 0.020 dm^3, which is 0.25 mol dm^-3.

questions.stem: 0.45 g of a dibasic acid, H2X, exactly neutralised 100 cm^3 of 0.10 mol dm^-3 sodium hydroxide. What is the molar mass of the acid?
questions.explanation: NaOH = 0.010 mol, so H2X = 0.0050 mol, and the molar mass = 0.45/0.0050 = 90 g mol^-1. 45 ignores the basicity.

questions.stem: What steady current must flow for 30 minutes to deposit 0.635 g of copper from a copper(II) salt solution? (Cu = 63.5; F = 96 500 C mol^-1)
questions.explanation: Cu = 0.010 mol, which needs 0.020 mol of electrons = 1930 C. I = 1930/1800 s = 1.07 A. 64.3 A comes from using minutes instead of seconds.

questions.stem: What mass of aluminium is deposited by 2.0 faradays of electricity during the electrolysis of molten alumina? (Al = 27)
questions.explanation: Al3+ + 3e- -> Al, so 3 F deposit 27 g and 2 F deposit 18 g.

questions.stem: What volume of chlorine, measured at s.t.p., is given off at the anode when 9650 C of electricity passes through concentrated brine? (F = 96 500 C mol^-1; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3)
The bond energies are: H-H = 436 kJ mol^-1, Cl-Cl = 242 kJ mol^-1 and H-Cl = 431 kJ mol^-1. What is the enthalpy change for H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2HCl(g)?
questions.explanation: Bonds broken = 436 + 242 = 678 kJ. Bonds formed = 2 x 431 = 862 kJ. dH = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ mol^-1.

questions.stem: The enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is -1370 kJ mol^-1. What mass of ethanol must be burnt to release 685 kJ of heat? (C2H5OH = 46 g mol^-1)
For a reaction, dH = -100 kJ mol^-1 and dS = -0.20 kJ mol^-1 K^-1. Above what temperature does the reaction stop being spontaneous?
questions.explanation: dG = dH - TdS becomes zero when T = dH/dS = -100/-0.20 = 500 K. Above this temperature the -TdS term makes dG positive.

questions.stem: For the reaction A + B -> products, doubling the concentration of A doubles the rate, and doubling the concentration of B makes the rate four times faster. By what factor does the rate increase if the concentrations of both A and B are doubled?
questions.explanation: The effects multiply: 2 x 4 = 8.

questions.stem: A flask containing marble chips and acid lost 2.2 g in mass in the first 100 s as carbon(IV) oxide escaped. What was the average rate of production of CO2 in mol s^-1? (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 2.2/44 = 0.050 mol of CO2 in 100 s, which is 5.0 x 10^-4 mol s^-1.

questions.stem: In which of these equilibria will BOTH an increase in pressure AND a decrease in temperature increase the yield of product?
options: CaCO3(s) <=> CaO(s) + CO2(g); dH = +178 kJ mol^-1
questions.explanation: The product side must have fewer gas moles (4 -> 2) and the forward reaction must be exothermic. Pressure has no effect on the HI equilibrium.

questions.stem: In the balanced equation Cu + xHNO3 -> Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: N: 2 in Cu(NO3)2 + 2 in NO2 = 4. O check: 12 = 6 + 4 + 2. H check: 4 = 2 x 2.

questions.stem: In the reaction 2KMnO4 + 16HCl -> 2KCl + 2MnCl2 + 5Cl2 + 8H2O, the oxidation number of manganese
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 in KMnO4 to +2 in MnCl2, a decrease of 5, so it is reduced.

questions.stem: Radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting three alpha particles and two beta particles. What are the mass number (A) and atomic number (Z) of the nucleus that forms?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. A piece of ancient wood has one-eighth of the carbon-14 activity of living wood. How old is the wood?
questions.explanation: 1/8 = (1/2)^3, so three half-lives have passed: 3 x 5730 = 17 190 years.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are there in the sulphide ion, 32/16 S 2- (mass number 32, atomic number 16)?
questions.explanation: Protons = 16, neutrons = 32 - 16 = 16, and a 2- charge means 2 extra electrons, giving 18.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: What is the mass of one atom of carbon-12? (Avogadro constant = 6.0 x 10^23 mol^-1)
questions.explanation: 12 g contains 6.0 x 10^23 atoms, so one atom has a mass of 12/(6.0 x 10^23) = 2.0 x 10^-23 g.

questions.stem: What volume of oxygen, measured at s.t.p., is needed to burn 0.10 mol of propane completely? C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3)
questions.explanation: 0.10 mol of C3H8 needs 0.50 mol of O2, and 0.50 x 22.4 = 11.2 dm^3. 6.72 dm^3 is the volume of CO2 formed.

questions.stem: An alkene has a relative molecular mass of 70. What is its molecular formula? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Alkenes are CnH2n, so Mr = 14n. 14n = 70 gives n = 5, so the formula is C5H10. C5H12 is an alkane.

questions.stem: What mass of ethanol can be obtained from the complete fermentation of 90 g of glucose? C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2 (C6H12O6 = 180, C2H5OH = 46)
questions.explanation: 90/180 = 0.50 mol of glucose, which gives 1.0 mol of ethanol = 46 g.

questions.stem: What is the name of the ester formed when propanoic acid reacts with methanol?
questions.explanation: The alcohol gives the first part of the name (methyl), and the acid gives the -oate part (propanoate).

questions.stem: What mass of water of crystallisation is contained in 24.95 g of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) pentahydrate, CuSO4.5H2O? (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Mr = 249.5, so 24.95 g = 0.10 mol. This contains 0.50 mol of H2O = 9.0 g. 15.95 g is the mass of anhydrous CuSO4.

questions.stem: What volume of chlorine, measured at s.t.p., is produced when 8.7 g of manganese(IV) oxide reacts with excess concentrated hydrochloric acid? MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2 (Mn = 55, O = 16; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3)
questions.explanation: MnO2 = 87 g/mol, so 8.7 g = 0.10 mol, which gives 0.10 mol of Cl2 = 2.24 dm^3.

questions.stem: What volume of ammonia, measured at s.t.p., can be obtained by heating 10.7 g of ammonium chloride with excess calcium hydroxide? (N = 14, H = 1, Cl = 35.5; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm^3)
questions.explanation: NH4Cl = 53.5 g/mol, so 10.7 g = 0.20 mol, which gives 0.20 mol of NH3 = 4.48 dm^3.

questions.stem: A PVC chain is made up of 500 chloroethene (CH2=CHCl) units. What is its relative molecular mass? (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5)
questions.explanation: Chloroethene has Mr = 24 + 3 + 35.5 = 62.5, and 62.5 x 500 = 31 250.

questions.stem: Which equation shows how washing soda removes permanent hardness from water?
questions.explanation: The Ca2+ ions are precipitated as insoluble CaCO3. The second equation shows temporary hardness being removed by boiling.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: The first four ionisation energies of an element X are 738, 1451, 7733 and 10 540 kJ mol^-1. In which group of the periodic table is X?
questions.explanation: The large jump comes after the second electron is removed, so X has 2 valence electrons. (X is magnesium.)

questions.explanation: The sun's heat evaporates the water and leaves the salt behind.

options: They have a pH greater than 7
questions.explanation: Sourness (as in lemons and vinegar) is typical of acids. The other properties belong to alkalis.

questions.stem: Which of these changes would slow down a chemical reaction?
options: Grinding a solid reactant into powder
Increasing the concentration of the reactants
questions.explanation: At a lower temperature, fewer collisions have the activation energy needed for reaction.

questions.stem: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Potassium is near the top of the reactivity series. Copper and silver are near the bottom.

questions.stem: What is the simplest alkane?
questions.explanation: Methane, CH4, has one carbon atom. Ethene is an alkene, not an alkane.

questions.stem: What is the monomer of polythene?
questions.explanation: Polythene is made by the addition polymerisation of ethene. Chloroethene gives PVC.

questions.explanation: Cations (positive ions) move to the cathode and gain electrons there.

questions.explanation: In a covalent bond the shared pair of electrons is attracted to both nuclei.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Which particle in the nucleus of an atom carries no charge?
questions.explanation: Neutrons are neutral. Protons are positive, and electrons, which are outside the nucleus, are negative.

questions.stem: What colour is chlorine gas?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a greenish-yellow gas. Bromine vapour is reddish-brown and iodine vapour is violet.

questions.explanation: Propane and butane liquefy easily under moderate pressure, so they can be stored in cylinders.
